exceptions.reason: Published 2026-10-05: the unsafe-operation guard does not block git trailer command configuration. simple-git 3.36.0 is installed and the fix is in the 4.x line only. It is installed only beneath @wordpress/env (a devDependency), which uses it in two places: lib/download-sources.js, to clone and update the git sources named in a wp-env configuration, and lib/runtime/docker/download-wp-phpunit.js, to clone the WordPress test suite from a GitHub address written in that file. @wordpress/env 11.16.0, the latest release, requires simple-git ^3.32.3 and calls the package as a function (`require( 'simple-git' )( … )`). simple-git 4, where the fixes are, exports an object with a named `simpleGit` instead, so overriding it does not install a fix, it breaks `wp-env start`: the override was tried on 2026-10-07 and wp-env's own call sequence failed at the first line with "SimpleGit is not a function".
exceptions.control: The defect is a way round simple-git's refusal of dangerous git options, so it matters where somebody else chooses the arguments, the configuration or the environment simple-git is given. Here they come from one place: wp-env.json in this repository, which names a single git source, `WordPress/WordPress#master`, and the fixed option objects in wp-env's source. A person who can change that file can already run any command on the same machine through wp-env's documented `lifecycleScripts`, so the advisory gives them nothing they lack. It runs only when a developer starts wp-env (`npm run env:start`); no workflow under .github/ uses wp-env, and scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and never node_modules, so it reaches neither CI nor a WordPress site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/env publishes a release that depends on simple-git 4.0.1 or later; a lockfile update then takes it with no override. Re-argue instead of renewing if wp-env.json gains a source whose URL or ref is not written in this repository, or if a CI workflow starts using wp-env: either would end the reasoning above.

exceptions.reason: Published 2026-10-19: a glob made of one repeated extglob branch, such as `+(*)` or `+(*a)`, is skipped by analyzeRepeatedExtglob in lib/parse.js and compiles to a regular expression that backtracks exponentially on a short crafted string. Every published version is affected: the advisory covers `<=4.0.7`, 4.0.7 is the latest release, and no patched version exists, so neither an upgrade nor an override can remove it (DECISIONS #648). In the root it is installed six times (2.3.2 at the top, 4.0.5 and 4.0.7 nested), all under devDependencies: micromatch and anymatch for fast-glob, globby, stylelint, http-proxy-middleware and jest-haste-map; the jest packages for test discovery; tinyglobby for @typescript-eslint, eslint-import-resolver-typescript, markdownlint-cli and webpack-dev-server; and @parcel/watcher. The lockfile marks the top-level 2.3.2 devOptional, not dev, for the reason #648 checked: @wordpress/theme, beneath @wordpress/components, lists stylelint as an optional peer, and the build maps @wordpress/components to WordPress's own script.
exceptions.control: The defect needs the attacker to choose the glob pattern; matching a crafted path against a fixed pattern does not trigger it. It runs on developer machines and CI runners in `npm run lint:js`, `npm run lint:css`, `npm run test:js` and `npm run build`, and the patterns it compiles come from the Jest, ESLint, stylelint and webpack configuration and the package.json scripts in this repository. No tracked file in this repository imports picomatch, micromatch, anymatch, tinyglobby, fdir, fast-glob or globby, so every pattern comes from a tool's own source or from configuration and script arguments committed here. Supplying one therefore means committing to this repository's tooling configuration, which already grants code execution in the same job, and the worst result is one stalled process. No glob library reaches a WordPress site or a server: scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and never node_modules, and the docs build is a static site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when picomatch publishes a release outside `<=4.0.7` and the advisory names it: an override or lockfile update then takes it. Re-argue instead of renewing if a tracked file starts calling a glob library with a pattern it did not write, or if any of these packages reaches a running server or a shipped build.
